name: Cy5–COT (Altman 2012)
description: The first self-healing dye: COT on a flexible tether from one indolenine nitrogen. Cy5's triplet lifetime drops from 63 to ~1 µs and photobleaching slows 2-70×. Linker atoms illustrative.

name: Gentle Rhodamine GR555-mito (TMR–COT)
description: TMR with COT esterified onto the pendant ring's carboxyl (COT–CH2–O–C(=O)–Ar): 10× less singlet oxygen than TMRM and 4-5× less phototoxicity (Liu et al. 2024).

name: Self-healing JF525 (JF525–phenylene–carotenoid)
description: JF525 with a photosystem-style triplet quencher: a 1,4-phenylene (the TTA Flora linker) on the pendant ring, para to the xanthene, carrying 7'-apo-β-carotene. Both carboxyls are kept (lactone, HaloTag handle). Our design; see README for why its singlet levels need checking.

name: LHCII: chlorophylls + carotenoids (1RWT)
description: Nature's self-healing antenna: plant light-harvesting complex II, 14 chlorophylls and 4 carotenoids held by the protein (faint). Lutein 620 lies 3.6 Å from Chl a610 and takes its triplets. No covalent linker: the protein holds them in contact.

name: Chlorophyll + carotenoid pair (Chl a610 + Lutein 620)
description: Just the two pigments, cut out of LHCII at their crystal positions: the chlorophyll that makes most triplets and the lutein lying across it (3.6 Å apart) that takes them. No linker, no protein.

name: Cy5–(phenylene)n–COT (our design)
description: COT on Cy5's benzo ring (C5, where sulfo-Cy5 has a sulfonate) at the end of a rigid rod of n 1,4-phenylenes, the TTA Flora linker. n = 0 bonds COT straight to the dye. No published analogue found.
